original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Exact simultaneous full-leading-minor header density for commuting corank-one P=I-U,Q=I-V with orthogonal rank-one kernels over finite fields. General finite-state transfer law and a binary all-dimension closed form with strict negative correlation.
scope_change_reason: This is original counting work answering a concrete subcase of the nonorthogonal full-guard question in PR4240 and PR4246, rather than an independent audit of PR4100. It changes the card premise and is a side result, not supplier admission.
bottleneck_link: Shared-header pricing needs joint guard laws, not products of marginal probabilities. The exact count specifies one overlapping-image case; physical caller costs and a real producer remain unknown, so kappa is unchanged.
stop_rule: Prove the transfer reduction and binary formula, compare both with complete small header and normalized-pair censuses, then stop without expanding into a physical caller.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the general transfer theorem and binary closed form. verify.py enumerates all normalized pairs in 12 finite domains and all complete GL headers in seven domains, with independent literal no-pivot elimination, 99 transfer cases and four controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can the transfer law be reduced to a closed form or a smaller invariant state space for odd q?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Odd fields lie in the retained executable normalizer domain, and a compact formula would expose the exact dependence there.
open_questions.first_step: Diagonalize or quotient the q=3 transfer matrix while preserving both diagonal guard values and the rank of I-A.
open_questions.blocked_by: No invariant-state lumping is proved here.

open_questions.question: What is the joint full-guard law for more than two corank-one requests with pairwise orthogonal rank-one kernels?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would determine whether a shared header can serve a larger overlapping family.
open_questions.first_step: Replace the 2 by 2 partial Gram matrix by a 3 by 3 matrix for q=2 and m=3,4.
open_questions.blocked_by: The binary four-state simplification no longer applies.

open_questions.question: Does an actual odd-field request producer admit a fully charged shared-header caller?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A joint density is not a physical saving.
open_questions.first_step: Pin a producer with orthogonal kernel lines and charge header selection, emission, dispatch, dirty return and stock.
open_questions.blocked_by: No producer or complete physical invoice is supplied.
